findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "browse_locations" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List the US states that have exotic car rental listings, or the cities of one state, with the number of cars and companies and the lowest published daily rate i…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_companies, get_news_article, search, fetch · Private data: search_vehicles, get_company, vehicle_availability, fetch · Public sink: search_vehicles, search_companies, price_overview.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_companies, get_news_article, search, fetch · Private data: search_vehicles, get_company, vehicle_availability, fetch · Public sink: search_vehicles, search_companies, price_overview

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
